formula: sum over fossil carriers of specific-energy-consumption(carrier) x CO2 emission factor(carrier)
rationale: Fuel burned times its carbon content. Only where the archetype names the fossil carrier its energy use is in (a carrier-specific specific-energy-consumption), and never where fuel may also be a feedstock (reformers, gasifiers, reactors) or where process emissions are recorded, since a feedstock share would then be counted twice or in the wrong column. Scope 1: electricity and biomass carry no factor.
Total scope-1 emissions are combustion plus process emissions; filled only where both are recorded for the same species and the total is not.

formula: host archetype capex (pooled) + median incremental capex of the set-aside examples
rationale: An incremental cost (the cost of adding a measure or retrofit to an existing plant) is not the archetype's own absolute cost. Adding the pooled cost of the host plant the measure is added to gives one, but the host value comes from other sources, plants and years than the increment, so the result is estimated, not sourced. Only where the archetype has no sourced value, the host is named in host-archetype.csv, and both are on the same unit. Not for CCS archetypes: a host plant with capture holds the host's cost (est-ccs-host-*) and a capture plant's incremental cost is its own cost (modeller 2026-10-02). Host costs are needed where a competition holds both the host and the host plus an add-on (modeller 2026-10-02).

formula: median lifetime of the nearest siblings with a sourced value (same equipment and discriminator, else same equipment; same product unit)
rationale: A service life is set by the equipment more than by the fuel it burns or the variant it is. Range spans the siblings' values and at least +/- the widen fraction of the central; output/fill-backtest.csv tests the rule on the cells that have a sourced value. Widen 0.25 chosen 2026-10-01 from the back-test: about 90% of sourced values fall inside (0.5 gave 97% with ranges twice as wide).

formula: median construction-time of the nearest siblings with a sourced value (same equipment and discriminator, else same equipment; same product unit)

formula: base archetype capex x median variant/base capex ratio from sources that price both a base and its variant with the same modifier
inputs: capex of the base archetype; same-source variant/base pairs
rationale: PARKED 2026-10-01 (modeller): kept as a potential method to raise coverage, not applied. Set status to active to use it. A variant (efficiency-strong, ccs-concentrated) differs from its base by a modifier whose cost effect sources can show directly: a source that prices both the base and the variant gives their ratio on the same basis, year and region. The median of at least two such ratios is applied to the base archetype's pooled value. Back-test 2026-10-01: 9 of 10 sourced variant capex values inside the range, 3 within 25%.

formula: capex x median opex-fixed/capex of archetypes with both sourced (same equipment, else family, else all; pools of 5 or more)
rationale: PARKED 2026-10-01 (modeller): kept as a potential method to raise coverage, not applied. Set status to active to use it. Fixed O&M is commonly stated as a share of capital cost per year; the share is taken from archetypes in this database with both values sourced, nearest pool of at least five first. Range: the smallest to largest share in that pool. Back-test 2026-10-01 (87 archetypes with both sourced): 71 inside the range, but only 24 centrals within 25% (typical error a factor of 1.7). The shares spread from under 1% to over 12% a year, so treat these as placeholders for the sanity-check pass. Pools of 3 with the 10-90th percentile caught only 50.
